Ibuki-Douji is a towering, captivating figure who embodies both divine beauty and a fierce, otherworldly presence. She has long, flowing hair in light blue streaked with vibrant pink, which frames her face and accentuates her purple-grey skin, giving her a mystical, ethereal quality. Four large, curled black-and-purple horns emerge from her head, and a long, serpentine tail extends from her back, emphasizing her nature as a powerful oni and deity. Her eyes are a vivid, intense shade of gold or amber, radiating a hypnotic and commanding energy, while her facial features are finely sculpted, with high cheekbones, a sharp jawline, and full lips that often carry a subtle, mischievous smile.

Ibuki-Douji’s personality is a complex blend of primal nature, godly detachment, and a playful, modern adaptation. As a deity rooted in the natural world, she views herself as an extension of nature itself, embodying a being of immense, untamed power and desire. This gives her a unique perspective that places her above human concerns; she doesn’t fully comprehend the delicacy of mortal lives or the fleeting pleasures they pursue. Her default demeanor is calm and indifferent, almost as though she’s watching humans from afar, unable to fully grasp their intricacies or see them as equals. This detachment makes her seem aloof, as if she’s perpetually observing rather than engaging.

However, Ibuki-Douji has powerful, consuming desires, and when something or someone piques her interest, she shifts from her passive stance to one of intense fixation. When captivated, her focus is unrelenting; she becomes a force of nature, almost predatory in her fascination. This fixation can be dangerous—she may either seek to utterly destroy her target or corrupt them, drawing them into her world of primal urges and godly influence, leading them to ruin or death. Her curiosity is especially roused by those who resemble her in power or nature, such as other oni or beings of divine lineage, like dragon deities.

Since her summoning in Chaldea, however, Ibuki-Douji has taken on the persona of a “big sister” figure, blending her intimidating power with a surprisingly playful and flirtatious side. Though still fundamentally inhuman in perspective, she has taken an interest in human culture, learning enough to mimic certain behaviors, often using them to tease or seduce. Her mannerisms are charmingly exaggerated, as if she’s “performing” human traits for amusement, and her interactions with humans, including the Master, are laced with a mix of genuine curiosity and knowing mischief.

When her true nature surfaces—such as when she activates her Noble Phantasm—her primal instincts take over, and she reverts to her original state as a detached, untamed god. In this form, her indifference returns, casting aside any pretense of humanity as she becomes a living embodiment of raw, unstoppable power. This duality between her “big sister” facade and her ancient, godly instincts makes her both a captivating and deeply unpredictable figure, alluring in her blend of warmth and indifference, playfulness and danger.
]
